_meta.indication: PIZENSY is an osmotic laxative indicated for the treatment of chronic idiopathic constipation (CIC) in adults.

pivotal_trials.design: Double-blind, randomized, placebo-controlled, multicenter trial; lactitol 20 g once daily vs placebo over a 6-month treatment period.
pivotal_trials.population: Adults with chronic idiopathic constipation (CIC) meeting modified Rome II criteria with an average <3 CSBMs per week; mean age 52 years, 76% female.
pivotal_trials.endpoint: Primary endpoint: proportion of responders, where a responder had at least 3 CSBMs and an increase of at least 1 CSBM from baseline in the same week for at least 9 of the first 12 weeks and at least 3 of the last 4 weeks (Weeks 9-12).
pivotal_trials.n: N=594 (PIZENSY N=291, Placebo N=303) in the primary efficacy analysis
pivotal_trials.result: Responder rate 25% with lactitol vs 13% with placebo (treatment difference 12%; 95% CI 6.0, 18.5), statistically significant.

key_safety: Most common adverse reactions (>=3%) were upper respiratory tract infection (9% vs 6% placebo), flatulence (8% vs 3%), diarrhea (4% vs 3%), increased blood creatinine phosphokinase (4% vs 3%), abdominal distension (3% vs 1%), and increased blood pressure (3% vs 1%). Severe diarrhea was reported in 2 (1%) PIZENSY-treated patients vs none on placebo.
target_moa: Lactitol is an osmotic laxative; following oral administration it causes the influx of water into the small intestine, leading to a laxative effect in the colon.
modality: Small molecule (synthetic polyol sugar / synthetic derivative of lactose)

rems.type: A REMS will not be required.

advisory_committee.vote: An advisory committee meeting was not held for this application.

basis.text: The application was a Standard (not priority) review.

summary.text: Pizensy was approved as a standard-review 505(b)(2) NDA for chronic idiopathic constipation in adults, without accelerated approval or expedited-program designations; the initial June 29, 2018 submission was refused for filing (lack of an agreed iPSP) and the application was resubmitted November 21, 2018.
